summary: Work packages must follow the Deloitte WBS table: a 3-level hierarchy (levels 1–3) with codes like 1.0, 1.1, 1.1.1. Each row is one element.

columns.description: Accountable party (maps to RACI A): Client or Consultant who owns delivery of this element. Use Joint only when accountability is genuinely shared. Supporting parties belong in the RACI matrix, not here.

hierarchy_rules: Level 1 = phase / major deliverable (WBS code X.0).
Level 2 = work stream under that phase (X.Y).
Level 3 = task under a work stream (X.Y.Z).
parent_wbs_code must reference an existing wbs_code one level above.
Minimum 3 level-1 elements, each with at least 2 level-2 children.
Also include owner, estimated_duration, and dependencies (list of wbs_codes).
Also include owner_side for each row: Client, Consultant, or Joint.
Prefer Client or Consultant over Joint — assign the party that is accountable (RACI A) for the work being done.
Do not use Joint as a default when one party clearly leads or holds the pen (RACI R/A).
Supporting roles (who helps the responsible party) are captured in the RACI matrix, not in owner_side.
generation_rules: owner_side indicates who is accountable for the work package (RACI A), not who supports delivery.
Assign Client or Consultant whenever one side clearly leads; reserve Joint for genuinely shared accountability.
Set `owner` to the named role or person who holds the pen (RACI R) when known from the brief.
Provide `estimated_duration` on level-2 and level-3 items to support milestone scheduling in the status report.

example_rows.wbs_element_title: Uptown Yonge BIA Streetscape Master Plan
example_rows.description_scope: Complete project scope for developing a long-term streetscape vision and implementation plan for Uptown Yonge BIA.
Manage project scope, schedule, communication, meetings, quality control, and coordination with the BIA and City staff.
Confirm project objectives, study area, roles, schedule, communication process, and approval pathway.
Provide regular updates to the BIA Board, Streetscape Committee, Executive Director, and City Staff Working Group.
Review all reports, drawings, cost estimates, and presentation materials before submission.
Review existing conditions, development plans, transit plans, City policies, design guidelines, and regulatory constraints.
Review City of Toronto policies, transportation standards, public realm guidelines, accessibility requirements, and BIA-related guidance.
